steps.body: **Sort** things into groups that match — then **count** each group! Buttons by color: 4 red, 3 blue.

widget.prompt: Sort each toy into its group.

items.label: teddy bear
items.feedback: A bear is an animal friend.

items.label: toy car
items.feedback: Cars drive — into the vehicle group.

widget.missFeedback: Ask: is it an animal, or does it drive?

steps.body: After sorting, **count** each group. Counting tells which group is biggest!

explanationVariants: Count each group: 5 spoons, 3 forks — spoons are more.
5 is more than 3, so the spoon group is bigger.

widget.prompt: You sort silverware: 5 spoons and 3 forks. Tap the group with more.

hotspots.label: 3 forks
hotspots.feedback: 3 is fewer than 5 — SPOONS are more.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents sort and count.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for sort and count must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines sort and count.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

items.label: mouse
items.feedback: A mouse fits in a hand — small group.

items.label: ladybug
items.feedback: A ladybug sits on a fingertip — small group.

widget.missFeedback: Ask: is it giant, or could you hold it?
widget.successFeedback: Sorted by size — giants together, tiny friends together!

explanationVariants: A red apple joins the red group when sorting by color, and the food group when sorting by kind — sorts can change!
The rule decides the group: color rule → red; kind rule → food.

widget.prompt: You sort by COLOR, then sort again by KIND. Where does a red apple go each time?

options.label: Red group first, then food group
options.feedback: Yes — the sorting rule decides the group.

options.label: Red group both times
options.feedback: The second sort is by KIND — the apple joins the food group.

options.label: Food group both times
options.feedback: The first sort is by COLOR — red group first.

options.label: It cannot be sorted twice
options.feedback: It can! New rule, new group — red, then food.

explanationVariants: 2 red and 4 blue buttons make 6 in all — sorting does not change the total.

widget.prompt: You sort 6 buttons into 2 red and 4 blue. The 2 red are already in the frame. Add the blue ones — how many buttons in ALL?

commonCounts.feedback: That is just the blue group — ALL means both: 6.
That is just the red group — together they are 6.
Sorting never adds buttons — 2 and 4 still make 6.

widget.missFeedback: Sorting never loses a button — the red 2 and blue 4 together fill the frame to 6.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — 2 and 4 joined back make 6. Sorting never loses any!

steps.body: Match the sorting rule to the right group.
explanationVariants: The rule picks the group: by color the red apple goes with red things; by kind it goes with food.
Same apple, new rule, new group — color puts it with red, kind puts it with food, and the car by kind goes with things that drive.

widget.prompt: Match each item and sorting rule to its group.

left.label: a red apple, sorted by color
a red apple, sorted by kind
a toy car, sorted by kind

pairErrors.feedback: That would work for color. Here the rule is kind, so an apple goes with food.

widget.missFeedback: Read the sorting rule before choosing the group.
widget.successFeedback: Great sorting — the same item can move when the rule changes!

hints: Read the rule first: is it color or kind?
A red apple sorted by color goes with red things.
Sorted by kind, the apple goes with food and the car goes with things that drive.

steps.body: Sort into matching groups, count each, compare — the whole course in one move!
takeaways: Sort by a rule: color, kind, or size.
Count each group to compare them.
steps.teaser: That completes Shapes & Sorting — Kindergarten math, done!

concept.body: Sort things into matching groups, then count each group. The biggest count is the biggest group.

explanationVariants: 2 cats and 5 dogs: 5 is more, so dogs are the bigger group.

widget.prompt: You sort pets: 2 cats and 5 dogs. Which group is bigger?

options.label: Cats
options.feedback: 2 is fewer — DOGS (5) are the bigger group.

options.label: Cannot tell
options.feedback: The counts tell you: 5 > 2, dogs win.
